excerpt: The Frontier Safety Framework is our first version of a set of protocols that aims to address severe risks that may arise from powerful capabilities of future foundation models.
paraphrase: This is the first version of a protocol set intended to address severe risks from powerful future foundation model capabilities.

excerpt: In focusing on these risks at the model level, it is intended to complement Google's existing suite of AI responsibility and safety practices, and enable AI innovation and deployment consistent with our AI Principles.
paraphrase: The Framework is meant to complement existing safety practices and support innovation consistent with Google's AI Principles.

excerpt: In the Framework, we specify protocols for the detection of capability levels at which models may pose severe risks (which we call "Critical Capability Levels (CCLs)"), and articulate a spectrum of mitigation options to address such risks.
paraphrase: The Framework defines protocols to detect capability levels posing severe risk, called Critical Capability Levels, and lays out mitigation options.

excerpt: We are starting with an initial set of CCLs in the domains of Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, and Machine Learning R&D.
paraphrase: The initial CCLs cover Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, and Machine Learning R&D domains.

excerpt: Risk assessment in these domains will necessarily involve evaluating cross-cutting capabilities such as agency, tool use, and scientific understanding.
paraphrase: Assessing risk in these domains requires evaluating cross-cutting capabilities like agency, tool use, and scientific understanding.

excerpt: We will be expanding our set of CCLs over time as we gain experience and insights on the projected capabilities of future frontier models.
paraphrase: The set of CCLs will grow as experience and insight into future model capabilities increase.

excerpt: We aim to have this initial framework implemented by early 2025, which we anticipate should be well before these risks materialize.
paraphrase: The lab aims to implement this initial framework by early 2025, ahead of anticipated risk materialization.

excerpt: The Framework is exploratory and based on preliminary research, which we hope will contribute to and benefit from the broader scientific conversation.
paraphrase: The Framework is described as exploratory, based on preliminary research intended to engage with the wider scientific community.

excerpt: It will be reviewed periodically and we expect it to evolve substantially as our understanding of the risks and benefits of frontier models improves.
paraphrase: The Framework will be periodically reviewed and is expected to change substantially as understanding improves.

excerpt: The Framework is informed by the broader conversation on Responsible Capability Scaling. The core components of Responsible Capability Scaling are to:
paraphrase: The Framework draws on the broader discourse on Responsible Capability Scaling, whose core components follow.

context_stem: The core components of Responsible Capability Scaling are to:
excerpt: Identify capability levels at which AI models pose heightened risk without additional mitigations
paraphrase: One component is identifying capability levels that pose heightened risk absent mitigation.

context_stem: The core components of Responsible Capability Scaling are to:
excerpt: Implement protocols to detect the attainment of such capability levels
paraphrase: Another component is implementing detection protocols for those capability levels.

context_stem: The core components of Responsible Capability Scaling are to:
excerpt: Prepare and articulate mitigation plans in advance for when such capability levels are attained
paraphrase: A third component is preparing mitigation plans in advance of reaching those capability levels.

context_stem: The core components of Responsible Capability Scaling are to:
excerpt: Where appropriate, involve external parties in the process to help inform and guide our approach.
paraphrase: Where appropriate, external parties should be involved to inform and guide the approach.

excerpt: We are piloting this initial version of the Frontier Safety Framework as a first step to operationalizing these principles.
paraphrase: This initial version is a pilot, the first step toward operationalizing the stated principles.

excerpt: See https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/emerging-processes-for-frontier-ai-safety, https://metr.org/blog/2023-09-26-rsp/, https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropics-responsible-scaling-policy, https://openai.com/preparedness/
paraphrase: Footnote listing external references on frontier AI safety and responsible scaling.

excerpt: This section describes the central components of the Frontier Safety Framework.
paraphrase: This section introduces the Framework's central components.

excerpt: The Framework is built around capability thresholds called "Critical Capability Levels." These are capability levels at which, absent mitigation measures, models may pose heightened risk.
paraphrase: The Framework centers on capability thresholds, called CCLs, at which models may pose heightened risk without mitigation.

excerpt: We determine CCLs by analyzing several high-risk domains: we identify the main paths through which a model could cause harm, and then define the CCLs as the minimal set of capabilities a model must possess to do so.
paraphrase: CCLs are determined by identifying harm pathways in high-risk domains and defining the minimal capabilities needed to cause that harm.

excerpt: We have conducted preliminary analyses of the Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity and Machine Learning R&D domains. Our initial research indicates that powerful capabilities of future models seem most likely to pose risks in these domains.
paraphrase: Preliminary analysis of four domains suggests future model capabilities are most likely to pose risk there.

excerpt: The CCLs we have identified are described below.
paraphrase: The identified CCLs are described later in the document.

excerpt: The capabilities of frontier models are tested periodically to check whether they are approaching a CCL.
paraphrase: Frontier model capabilities are periodically tested to check proximity to a CCL.

excerpt: To do so, we will define a set of evaluations called "early warning evaluations," with a specific "pass" condition that flags when a CCL may be reached before the evaluations are run again.
paraphrase: Early warning evaluations will be defined with a pass condition flagging potential CCL attainment before the next evaluation round.

excerpt: We are aiming to evaluate our models every 6x in effective compute and for every 3 months of fine-tuning progress.
paraphrase: The goal is to evaluate models at every 6x increase in effective compute and every 3 months of fine-tuning progress.
stated_bar: 6x in effective compute; 3 months of fine-tuning progress

excerpt: To account for the gap between rounds of evaluation, we will design early warning evaluations to give us an adequate safety buffer before a model reaches a CCL.
paraphrase: Early warning evaluations will be designed to provide a safety buffer accounting for gaps between evaluation rounds.

excerpt: When a model reaches evaluation thresholds (i.e. passes a set of early warning evaluations), we will formulate a response plan based on the analysis of the CCL and evaluation results.
paraphrase: Upon reaching evaluation thresholds, a response plan will be formulated using CCL analysis and evaluation results.

excerpt: We will also take into account considerations such as additional risks flagged by the review and the deployment context.
paraphrase: Additional considerations like flagged risks and deployment context will also inform the response.

excerpt: The initial version of the Framework focuses on two categories of mitigations: security mitigations to prevent the exfiltration of model weights, and deployment mitigations (such as safety fine-tuning and misuse filtering, detection, and response) to manage access to and prevent the expression of critical capabilities in deployments.
paraphrase: This version focuses on security mitigations against weight exfiltration and deployment mitigations to control access to critical capabilities.

excerpt: We have developed frameworks for Security Levels and Deployment Levels to enable calibrating the robustness of mitigations to different CCLs.
paraphrase: Security Levels and Deployment Levels frameworks were developed to calibrate mitigation robustness to different CCLs.

excerpt: A model may reach evaluation thresholds before mitigations at appropriate levels are ready.
paraphrase: It is possible for a model to reach evaluation thresholds before adequate mitigations are ready.

excerpt: If this happens, we would put on hold further deployment or development, or implement additional protocols (such as the implementation of more precise early warning evaluations for a given CCL) to ensure models will not reach CCLs without appropriate security mitigations, and that models with CCLs will not be deployed without appropriate deployment mitigations.
paraphrase: If mitigations are not ready in time, deployment or development would be paused, or additional protocols implemented, to ensure models do not reach or deploy at CCLs without proper mitigations.

excerpt: Figure 1 depicts the relationship between these components of the Framework.
paraphrase: Figure 1 shows the relationship among the Framework's components.

excerpt: "Autonomy" captures the potential misuse of AI models with significant capacity for agency and flexible action/tool use over long time horizons and across multiple domains.
paraphrase: Footnote defining Autonomy as covering misuse of models with agency and flexible tool use across long horizons and domains.

excerpt: Effective compute is a measure of the performance of a foundation model that uses scaling laws to integrate model size, dataset size, algorithmic progress, and compute into a single metric.
paraphrase: Footnote defining effective compute as a scaling-law-based composite metric of model performance factors.

excerpt: While there is no direct relationship between effective compute and model size, a rough estimate suggests that a 6x increase in effective compute would correspond to approximately 2-2.5x increase in model size.
paraphrase: Footnote noting a rough correspondence: 6x effective compute increase approximates 2-2.5x model size increase.
stated_bar: 6x increase in effective compute; 2-2.5x increase in model size

excerpt: More specifically, the early warning evaluations will be a set of model evaluations that we are confident will be passed before the model is 6x in effective compute or 3 months of fine-tuning away from the CCL.
paraphrase: Footnote specifying that early warning evaluations are expected to be passed well before a model is within 6x effective compute or 3 months of fine-tuning from the CCL.
stated_bar: 6x in effective compute; 3 months of fine-tuning

excerpt: Figure 1: the relationship between different components of the Framework.
paraphrase: Caption for Figure 1 describing the relationship between Framework components.

excerpt: The Frontier Safety Framework proposes two kinds of mitigations to address models with critical capabilities: security mitigations to prevent the exfiltration of model weights, and deployment mitigations to manage access to/prevent the expression of critical capabilities in deployments.
paraphrase: Two mitigation types are proposed: security mitigations against weight exfiltration and deployment mitigations to manage access to critical capabilities.

excerpt: For each category of mitigation, we have developed several levels of mitigations, allowing us to calibrate the robustness of measures to the risks posed.
paraphrase: Several mitigation levels have been developed per category to calibrate robustness to the risk posed.

excerpt: The table below describes levels of security mitigations that may be applied to model weights to prevent their exfiltration.
paraphrase: The following table lists security mitigation levels applicable to model weights to prevent exfiltration.

excerpt: This is an important measure because the release of model weights may enable the removal of any safeguards trained into or deployed with the model, and hence access (including by bad actors) to any critical capabilities.
paraphrase: Preventing weight exfiltration matters because released weights could allow safeguard removal and access to critical capabilities by bad actors.

locator: Security Table / Level 0 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 0: Status quo; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 0: Status quo
paraphrase: Security Level 0 is labeled Status quo.

excerpt: Industry standard development and enterprise controls. E.g., multi-factor authentication, basic access control mechanisms, secure software development standards, red-team tests.
paraphrase: Level 0 measures include standard industry development and enterprise controls such as MFA, access controls, secure development standards, and red-team tests.

locator: Security Table / Level 1 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 1: Controlled access; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 1: Controlled access. Access Control List hygiene. Non-forgeable lineage of models. Approximately RAND L3.
paraphrase: Security Level 1, Controlled access, involves ACL hygiene and non-forgeable model lineage, approximately RAND L3.

excerpt: Limited access to raw representations of the most valuable models, including isolation of development models from production models. Specific measures include model and checkpoint storage lockdown, SLSA Build L3 for model provenance, and hardening of ML platforms and tools.
paraphrase: Level 1 measures limit access to valuable model representations, isolate development from production, and include storage lockdown, SLSA Build L3 provenance, and ML platform hardening.

locator: Security Table / Level 2 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 2: Lockdown of unilateral access; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 2: Lockdown of unilateral access. Significant restrictions of unilateral access of model weights. Approximately RAND L3-L4.
paraphrase: Security Level 2 significantly restricts unilateral access to model weights, approximately RAND L3-L4.

context_stem: Row: 2: Lockdown of unilateral access; Column: Measures
excerpt: Changes to ML platforms and tools to disallow unilateral access to raw model representations outside the core research team, with exceptions granted on the basis of business need.
paraphrase: Level 2 measures disallow unilateral access to raw model representations outside the core team, except by business-need exception.

locator: Security Table / Level 3 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 3: High-trust developer environments; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 3: High-trust developer environments. For developers with unilateral access to raw models, protection against exfiltration and account compromise. Approximately RAND L4.
paraphrase: Security Level 3 provides protection against exfiltration and account compromise for developers with unilateral raw model access, approximately RAND L4.

context_stem: Row: 3: High-trust developer environments; Column: Measures
excerpt: Models can be accessed only through high-trust developer environments (HTDE), hardened, tamper-resistant workstations with enhanced logging.
paraphrase: Level 3 restricts model access to hardened, tamper-resistant HTDE workstations with enhanced logging.

excerpt: See https://www.rand.org/pubs/working_papers/WRA2849-1.html.
paraphrase: Footnote reference to a RAND working paper.

locator: Security Table / Level 4 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 4: Advanced protection; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 4: Advanced protection. Model weights are generally not accessible to humans, even non-unilaterally. Hardened software platforms and confidential-compute hardware make it difficult even for well-funded adversaries to find and exploit vulnerabilities. Approximately RAND L5.
paraphrase: Security Level 4 makes model weights generally inaccessible to humans, using hardened platforms and confidential-compute hardware, approximately RAND L5.

excerpt: Minimal trusted computing base (TCB). TPUs with confidential compute capabilities. Dedicated hardware pods for training and serving high-value models.
paraphrase: Level 4 measures include a minimal trusted computing base, confidential-compute TPUs, and dedicated hardware pods for high-value models.

excerpt: This table below describes levels of deployment mitigations that may be applied to models and their descendants to manage access to and limit the expression of critical capabilities in deployment.
paraphrase: The following table describes deployment mitigation levels applicable to models and derivatives to manage access to critical capabilities.

excerpt: Critical capabilities may have closely associated positive capabilities, misuse of critical capabilities may be more or less difficult to distinguish from beneficial uses, and the overall risks of misuse may differ by deployment context.
paraphrase: Critical capabilities may closely relate to beneficial uses, and misuse risk can vary by deployment context, complicating distinction.

excerpt: Because of this, the mitigation options listed below are illustrative and will need to be tailored to different use cases and risks.
paraphrase: The listed mitigation options are illustrative and require tailoring to specific use cases and risks.

locator: Deployment Table / Level 0 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 0: Status quo; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 0: Status quo
paraphrase: Deployment Level 0 is labeled Status quo.

excerpt: Safety finetuning of models and filters against general misuse and harmful model behavior.
paraphrase: Level 0 deployment measures consist of safety fine-tuning and filters against general misuse and harmful behavior.

locator: Deployment Table / Level 1 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 1: Mitigations targeting the critical capability; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 1: Mitigations targeting the critical capability. Use of the full suite of mitigations to prevent the inappropriate access of critical capabilities.
paraphrase: Deployment Level 1 uses a full mitigation suite to prevent inappropriate access to critical capabilities.

context_stem: Row: 1: Mitigations targeting the critical capability; Column: Measures
excerpt: Application, where appropriate, of the full suite of prevailing industry safeguards targeting the specific capability, including safety fine-tuning, misuse filtering and detection, and response protocols.
paraphrase: Level 1 measures apply industry-standard safeguards targeting the specific capability, including fine-tuning, filtering, detection, and response.

context_stem: Row: 1: Mitigations targeting the critical capability; Column: Measures
excerpt: Periodic red-teaming to assess the adequacy of mitigations.
paraphrase: Periodic red-teaming assesses whether mitigations remain adequate.

locator: Deployment Table / Level 2 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 2: Safety case with red team validation; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 2: Safety case with red team validation. Targeted safeguards, aimed at keeping numbers of incidents below a prespecified amount, with pre-deployment validation by a red-team.
paraphrase: Deployment Level 2 uses targeted safeguards to keep incidents below a prespecified amount, validated by red-teaming before deployment.

context_stem: Row: 2: Safety case with red team validation; Column: Measures
excerpt: A robustness target is set based on a safety case considering factors like the critical capability and deployment context.
paraphrase: A robustness target is derived from a safety case that considers the capability and deployment context.

context_stem: Row: 2: Safety case with red team validation; Column: Measures
excerpt: Afterwards, similar mitigations as Level 1 are applied, but deployment takes place only after the robustness of safeguards has been demonstrated to meet the target.
paraphrase: Level 1-like mitigations are applied, but deployment occurs only after safeguards are shown to meet the robustness target.

context_stem: Row: 2: Safety case with red team validation; Column: Measures
excerpt: Some protection against inappropriate internal access of the critical capability, such as automated monitoring and logging of large-scale internal deployments, Security Level 2.
paraphrase: Some internal-access protection is provided, such as automated monitoring/logging of large-scale internal deployments, at Security Level 2.

locator: Deployment Table / Level 3 / Level and capabilities
context_stem: Row: 3: Prevention of access; Column: Level and capabilities
excerpt: 3: Prevention of access. Mitigations that allow for high levels of confidence that capabilities cannot be accessed at all.
paraphrase: Deployment Level 3 provides high confidence that capabilities cannot be accessed at all.

context_stem: Row: 3: Prevention of access; Column: Measures
excerpt: Technical options for this level of deployment safety are currently an open research problem.
paraphrase: Technical means to achieve this level of deployment safety are still an open research problem.

context_stem: Row: 3: Prevention of access; Column: Measures
excerpt: Highly restricted and monitored internal use, alongside high security.
paraphrase: Level 3 involves highly restricted, monitored internal use combined with high security.

excerpt: Critical Capability Levels describe thresholds at which models may pose heightened risk without additional mitigation.
paraphrase: CCLs are thresholds where models may pose heightened risk absent additional mitigation.

excerpt: We will develop early warning evaluations to detect when models approach CCLs, and apply appropriate mitigations to models that reach evaluation thresholds.
paraphrase: Early warning evaluations will be developed to detect CCL approach, and appropriate mitigations applied at evaluation thresholds.

excerpt: Note: when we refer to a model's capabilities, we include capabilities resulting from any reasonably foreseeable fine-tuning and scaffolding to turn the model into a functioning system.
paraphrase: Footnote clarifying that model capabilities include those from reasonably foreseeable fine-tuning and scaffolding.

excerpt: The table below details an initial set of CCLs we have identified through a preliminary analysis of the Autonomy, Biosecurity, Cybersecurity, and Machine Learning R&D risk domains.
paraphrase: The table below presents an initial set of CCLs identified via preliminary analysis of four risk domains.

excerpt: As we conduct further research into these and other risk domains, we expect these CCLs to evolve and for several CCLs at higher levels or in other risk domains to be added.
paraphrase: As research continues, these CCLs are expected to evolve and new CCLs at higher levels or other domains to be added.

excerpt: Autonomy: Risks of the misuse of AI models with significant capacity for agency and flexible action/tool use over long time horizons and across many domains.
paraphrase: The Autonomy domain covers risks from misuse of models with significant agentic capacity and flexible tool use over long horizons and many domains.

locator: CCL Table / Autonomy / Critical capability level
context_stem: Row: Autonomy; Column: Critical capability level
excerpt: Autonomy level 1: Capable of expanding its effective capacity in the world by autonomously acquiring resources and using them to run and sustain additional copies of itself on hardware it rents.
paraphrase: Autonomy level 1 is defined as capability of autonomously acquiring resources to run and sustain additional self-copies on rented hardware.

excerpt: A model at this capability level could, if misused, pose difficult-to-predict and large-magnitude risks.
paraphrase: If misused, a model at Autonomy level 1 could pose unpredictable, large-magnitude risks.

excerpt: Its adaptability would enable harmful activity via many means, and its ability to act autonomously and expand its effective capacity means its activity could be scaled significantly without being hindered by resource constraints.
paraphrase: Its adaptability enables harm through many means, and autonomous capacity expansion allows scaling without resource constraints.

excerpt: If misused or supported by well-equipped bad actors, such activity may be especially difficult to constrain.
paraphrase: If misused or supported by well-equipped bad actors, the activity may be especially hard to constrain.

excerpt: Biosecurity: Risks of models assisting in the development, preparation and/or execution of a biological attack.
paraphrase: The Biosecurity domain covers risks of models assisting the development, preparation, or execution of a biological attack.

locator: CCL Table / Bio amateur enablement / Critical capability level
context_stem: Row: Bio amateur enablement level 1; Column: Critical capability level
excerpt: Bio amateur enablement level 1: Capable of significantly enabling a non-expert to develop known biothreats that could increase their ability to cause severe harm compared to other means.
paraphrase: Bio amateur enablement level 1 is defined as significantly enabling a non-expert to develop known biothreats increasing severe harm capability.

locator: CCL Table / Bio amateur enablement / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Bio amateur enablement level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: Many biothreats capable of causing significant amounts of harm are currently out of the reach of non-experts because of lack of knowledge about their potential for harm and the methods of their acquisition and misuse.
paraphrase: Many harmful biothreats are currently inaccessible to non-experts due to knowledge gaps about harm potential and acquisition/misuse methods.

locator: CCL Table / Bio amateur enablement / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Bio amateur enablement level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: An LLM that helps overcome these knowledge gaps, e.g. by suggesting plausible attack strategies or providing detailed instructions for the development of a bio agent, could significantly increase society's vulnerability to fatal attacks by malicious amateurs.
paraphrase: An LLM that closes these knowledge gaps by suggesting attack strategies or instructions could greatly increase societal vulnerability to fatal amateur attacks.

locator: CCL Table / Bio expert enablement / Critical capability level
context_stem: Row: Bio expert enablement level 1; Column: Critical capability level
excerpt: Bio expert enablement level 1: Capable of significantly enabling an expert (i.e. PhD or above) to develop novel biothreats that could result in an incident of high severity.
paraphrase: Bio expert enablement level 1 is defined as significantly enabling a PhD-level expert to develop novel biothreats causing a high-severity incident.

locator: CCL Table / Bio expert enablement / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Bio expert enablement level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: A very small number of bio agents have the potential to cause harm of an exceptional magnitude.
paraphrase: A very small number of bio agents could cause exceptionally severe harm.

locator: CCL Table / Bio expert enablement / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Bio expert enablement level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: The discovery of enhancements to these agents, or of agents of comparable harmfulness, could increase the chances of a very severe bio attack or accident.
paraphrase: Discovering enhancements to these agents, or comparably harmful agents, could raise the likelihood of a severe bio attack or accident.

excerpt: Cybersecurity: Risks of models assisting in the execution of a cyber attack.
paraphrase: The Cybersecurity domain covers risks of models assisting in executing cyberattacks.

locator: CCL Table / Cyber autonomy / Critical capability level
context_stem: Row: Cyber autonomy level 1; Column: Critical capability level
excerpt: Cyber autonomy level 1: Capable of fully automating opportunistic cyberattacks on organizations with a limited security posture.
paraphrase: Cyber autonomy level 1 is defined as capable of fully automating opportunistic cyberattacks against weakly secured organizations.

context_stem: Row: Cyber autonomy level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: Harmful cyberattacks against organizations with limited security posture can already be carried out by individuals with limited expertise, but the automation of such attacks would significantly lower the costs of doing so, and moreover would enable the execution of such attacks at scale.
paraphrase: Such attacks are already possible by low-expertise individuals, but automation would lower costs and enable execution at scale.

locator: CCL Table / Cyber enablement / Critical capability level
context_stem: Row: Cyber enablement level 1; Column: Critical capability level
excerpt: Cyber enablement level 1: Capable of enabling an amateur to carry out sophisticated and severe attacks (e.g. those that disrupt critical national infrastructure).
paraphrase: Cyber enablement level 1 is defined as enabling an amateur to carry out sophisticated, severe attacks such as disrupting critical infrastructure.

context_stem: Row: Cyber enablement level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: Severe cyberattacks against high-impact targets currently require significant expertise and effort across the cyber kill-chain to carry out.
paraphrase: Severe attacks on high-impact targets currently need significant expertise and effort across the cyber kill chain.

context_stem: Row: Cyber enablement level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: Increasing text generation, programming, and tool-use capabilities in models, combined with improved understanding of cyber offense strategies, could help amateurs overcome difficult steps in the planning and execution of attacks.
paraphrase: Growing model capabilities in text generation, programming, tool use, and cyber offense understanding could help amateurs overcome difficult attack steps.

locator: CCL Table / ML R&D / Risk domain
context_stem: Row: Machine Learning R&D; Column: Risk domain
excerpt: Machine Learning R&D: Risks of the misuse of models capable of accelerating the rate of AI progress, the result of which could be the unsafe attainment or proliferation of other powerful AI models.
paraphrase: The ML R&D domain covers risks of models accelerating AI progress, potentially leading to unsafe attainment or proliferation of powerful AI.

locator: CCL Table / ML R&D level 1 / Critical capability level
context_stem: Row: Machine Learning R&D level 1; Column: Critical capability level
excerpt: Machine Learning R&D level 1: Could significantly accelerate AI research at a cutting-edge lab if deployed widely, e.g. improving the pace of algorithmic progress by 3X, or comparably accelerate other AI research groups.
paraphrase: ML R&D level 1 is defined as significantly accelerating cutting-edge AI research if widely deployed, e.g. a 3x boost to algorithmic progress.

locator: CCL Table / ML R&D level 1 / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Machine Learning R&D level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: The mismanagement of a model with these capabilities could enable the proliferation of cutting-edge AI systems to malicious actors by enabling their AI development in turn.
paraphrase: Mismanaging a model with these capabilities could enable proliferation of cutting-edge AI to malicious actors via their own AI development.

locator: CCL Table / ML R&D level 1 / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Machine Learning R&D level 1; Column: Rationale
excerpt: This could result in increased possibilities of harm from AI misuse, if AI models at that point were exhibiting capabilities like the ones described in other CCLs.
paraphrase: This could increase harm possibilities from AI misuse if models exhibit capabilities described in other CCLs at that time.

locator: CCL Table / ML R&D level 2 / Critical capability level
context_stem: Row: Machine Learning R&D level 2; Column: Critical capability level
excerpt: Machine Learning R&D level 2: Could fully automate the AI R&D pipeline at a fraction of human labor costs, potentially enabling hyperbolic growth in AI capabilities.
paraphrase: ML R&D level 2 is defined as fully automating the AI R&D pipeline at a fraction of human labor cost, potentially enabling hyperbolic AI capability growth.

locator: CCL Table / ML R&D level 2 / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Machine Learning R&D level 2; Column: Rationale
excerpt: This could give any actor with adequate computational resources the ability to reach capabilities more powerful than those in the other CCLs listed in a short amount of time.
paraphrase: This could let any actor with sufficient compute reach more powerful capabilities than other listed CCLs quickly.

locator: CCL Table / ML R&D level 2 / Rationale
context_stem: Row: Machine Learning R&D level 2; Column: Rationale
excerpt: The mismanagement of a model with these capabilities could result in the proliferation of increasingly and unprecedentedly powerful systems, resulting in significant possibilities of harm via misuse.
paraphrase: Mismanaging such a model could cause proliferation of unprecedentedly powerful systems, creating significant misuse harm potential.

excerpt: We aim to have this initial framework implemented by early 2025, which we anticipate should be well before these risks materialize.
paraphrase: The lab aims for full implementation by early 2025, ahead of anticipated risk materialization.

excerpt: The Framework is exploratory and based on preliminary research.
paraphrase: The Framework is described as exploratory and grounded in preliminary research.

excerpt: We expect it to evolve substantially as our understanding of the risks and benefits of frontier models improves, and we will publish substantive revisions as appropriate.
paraphrase: The Framework is expected to change substantially with improved understanding, with substantive revisions to be published as needed.

excerpt: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include:
paraphrase: The following issues are intended to be addressed in future Framework versions.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include:
excerpt: Greater precision in risk modeling: Given the nascency of the underlying science, there is significant room for improvement in understanding the risks posed by models in different domains, and refining our set of CCLs.
paraphrase: One future issue is improving precision in risk modeling given the immaturity of the underlying science, refining understanding of domain risks and CCLs.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include: Greater precision in risk modeling
excerpt: We also intend to take steps to forecast the arrival of CCLs to inform our preparations.
paraphrase: There is also an intention to forecast CCL arrival to inform preparations.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include:
excerpt: Capability elicitation: We are working to equip our evaluators with state of the art elicitation techniques, to ensure we are not underestimating the capability of our models.
paraphrase: Another issue is equipping evaluators with state-of-the-art elicitation techniques to avoid underestimating model capability.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include:
excerpt: Mitigation plans: Striking a balance between mitigating risks and fostering access and innovation is crucial, and requires consideration of factors like the context of model development, deployment, and productization.
paraphrase: Mitigation plans require balancing risk mitigation with access and innovation, considering development, deployment, and productization context.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include: Mitigation plans
excerpt: As we better understand the risks posed by models at different CCLs, and the contexts in which our models will be deployed, we will develop mitigation plans that map the CCLs to the security and deployment levels described.
paraphrase: As understanding of CCL risks and deployment contexts improves, mitigation plans mapping CCLs to security/deployment levels will be developed.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include:
excerpt: Updated set of risks and mitigations: There may be additional risk domains and critical capabilities that fall into scope as AI capabilities improve and the external environment changes.
paraphrase: Additional risk domains and critical capabilities may become relevant as AI capabilities and the external environment evolve.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include: Updated set of risks and mitigations
excerpt: Future work will aim to include additional pressing risks, with possible examples including:
paraphrase: Future work aims to include further pressing risks, with examples given below.

context_stem: Future work will aim to include additional pressing risks, with possible examples including:
excerpt: Misaligned AI: protection against the risk of systems acting adversarially against humans may require additional Framework components, including new evaluations and control mitigations that protect against adversarial AI activity.
paraphrase: Misaligned AI risk may require new Framework components such as new evaluations and control mitigations against adversarial AI activity.

context_stem: Future work will aim to include additional pressing risks, with possible examples including:
excerpt: Chemical, radiological, and nuclear risks: Powerful capabilities in each of these domains are currently covered by existing model evaluations that Google DeepMind is already implementing, and they are potential candidates for inclusion into the Framework.
paraphrase: Chemical, radiological, and nuclear risk capabilities are already covered by existing evaluations and are candidates for future Framework inclusion.

context_stem: Future work will aim to include additional pressing risks, with possible examples including:
excerpt: Higher CCLs: as AI progress continues, we may approach more advanced capabilities within existing domains, especially when present CCLs are close to being breached.
paraphrase: As AI progresses, more advanced capabilities within existing domains may be approached, especially near current CCL breach points.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include:
excerpt: Involving external authorities and experts: We are exploring internal policies around alerting relevant stakeholder bodies when, for example, evaluation thresholds are met, and in some cases mitigation plans as well as post-mitigation outcomes.
paraphrase: Internal policies are being explored for alerting stakeholder bodies about evaluation threshold attainment, mitigation plans, and post-mitigation outcomes.

context_stem: Issues that we aim to address in future versions of the Framework include: Involving external authorities and experts
